fsPage.title: About Formula Student
fsPage.adaptNotice: This page describes the Formula Student competition in general. We still have to adapt the specifics to the Formula SAE Brazil rulebook — we'll fill that in as the project moves forward.

sections.title: What is Formula Student?
paragraphs: Formula Student is a global engineering design competition, where students from universities around the world develop and build their own single-seated racing cars.

However, winning is not all about building the fastest car. Victory belongs to the team which excels in all aspects: design, performance, cost planning, and business strategy. Teams are judged by experts from motorsport, automotive, and supplier industries, who assess both the technical quality of the car and the team's business approach.
Rules vary by country and organizing body within Formula Student. We'll be competing under the Formula SAE Brazil rulebook — we'll add the specific details here soon.

sections.title: Why do students build Formula-style cars?
paragraphs: Formula Student challenges students to go beyond their university coursework and apply their knowledge to a real-world project. It combines teamwork, time and project management, engineering, manufacturing, and business thinking.

By taking part, students gain valuable experience that's beneficial to them as future engineers. They also get more exposure to the automotive industry, since companies often use Formula Student as a platform to meet and recruit new talent.

sections.title: How do businesses and partners benefit?
paragraphs: Formula Student offers companies in the motorsport, automotive, and supplier industries a unique way to evaluate the skills of young engineers. By sponsoring or supporting teams, they can build early connections with highly motivated students.
Involvement as a judge, mentor, or sponsor also provides valuable insight into the next generation of engineering talent.

sections.title: The events of the competition
paragraphs: There are many Formula Student competitions around the world each year. While each has its own specialties, they all share the same core disciplines — the events in which teams must compete. These are split into two major categories: dynamic and static.

fsPage.dynamicIntro: Dynamic events test the performance of the cars on track. Each one evaluates a different physical feature of the vehicle: acceleration, skid pad, autocross, efficiency, and endurance.

dynamicEvents.title: Acceleration
dynamicEvents.body: The car's ability to accelerate is tested on a straight 75-metre stretch. Besides traction, powertrain design plays a major role, whether aiming for maximum output or strong torque delivery. The fastest cars complete the run in under four seconds and surpass 100 km/h before the finish line.

dynamicEvents.title: Skid Pad
dynamicEvents.body: Each car navigates a figure-eight circuit marked by cones, completing two laps per circle, of which the second lap is recorded. The result is comparable to the highest possible lateral acceleration. Many designs rely on aerodynamics to increase contact pressure and raise lateral speed. Hitting a cone leads to a time penalty.

dynamicEvents.title: Autocross
dynamicEvents.body: Cars run a course of roughly one kilometre that combines straights, bends, and tight chicanes. A strong lap reflects quick acceleration, precise steering, and effective braking. Hitting cones adds time as a penalty. Results in this event determine the starting order for endurance.

dynamicEvents.title: Efficiency
dynamicEvents.body: During the endurance event, the energy consumption of each car is carefully measured. What counts is not the amount of fuel or electricity used, but the usage relative to speed. This prevents teams from driving overly slowly to gain an advantage.

dynamicEvents.title: Endurance
dynamicEvents.body: As the most important challenge, endurance carries the most points. Cars must demonstrate their durability over a long course. Speed, agility, energy usage, and reliability are all judged. Drivers need good control, since several cars share the circuit at once. Only one attempt is allowed, with a mandatory driver swap halfway through.

fsPage.staticIntro: Static events focus on the teams' ability to handle the real-world hurdles of finance, business strategy, and sound engineering practice.

staticEvents.title: Design
staticEvents.body: Ahead of the competition, each team submits a detailed written description of their car, explaining its design and how it was applied in building the vehicle. Based on this submission, judges review the technical layout, design approach, and how effectively the concept was implemented in the final build. Afterwards, teams meet the panel in person to answer questions, defend their decisions, and show their depth of understanding. The evaluation considers not only the technical solution itself but also the reasoning behind it.

staticEvents.title: Cost
staticEvents.body: Since cost plays a central role in product development, this event challenges teams to show a full breakdown of their prototype. They must submit a cost report that includes parts, materials, and the manufacturing steps involved in production. The report is followed by a discussion with the judges, where teams explain their calculations and show they understand the practical aspects of building the car. Both the clarity of the report and the students' grasp of production processes are taken into account.

staticEvents.title: Presentation
staticEvents.body: Each team pitches a product or service directly related to the vehicle they built that season, as if presenting to potential investors. The goal is to convince the judges — acting as a fictitious company — that their concept meets the needs of a target market and could succeed commercially. The pitch is followed by a question round, where the team must respond confidently and adaptively. Both the content and structure of the presentation, as well as the team's delivery, are evaluated.

motorsportPage.title: The academy: three categories, one team
motorsportPage.intro: We're UTN BA's first Formula SAE generation, and we built it with three fronts running in parallel. Here's how each one works.

sections.title: Rookie
paragraphs: It all starts here: your first project inside the team is building a go-kart — a simple, concrete challenge to start building with your hands before you get into the single-seater.
Along the way you take your first steps into automotive engineering: welding, using tools like the lathe, and a first real look at the team's manufacturing processes.
No prior experience needed. This is the entry point to the team, built so anyone can join and grow.

sections.title: Baja SAE
paragraphs: Baja SAE isn't a rung on the Formula SAE ladder: it's a competition with its own SAE International technical rulebook, and our car isn't a formula single-seater but an off-road buggy-type vehicle.

Here, members train to work as professional motorsport demands: interpreting every requirement, documenting decisions, designing to pass inspections and using FIA/SFI-homologated components whenever required by the safety rules.

One detail that sets it apart from other competitions: every car uses the same engine, a Kohler Command Pro CH440 at roughly 10 HP with a restrictor plate. That takes horsepower out of the equation — the competition comes down 100% to design.

Static events judge design, cost analysis and a sales pitch in front of a panel, as if the car were a real product. Dynamic events put it to the test off-road: acceleration, hill climb, maneuverability, rock crawl and endurance.
It's an international SAE competition, with events in the United States, India (Baja SAEINDIA) and other countries.

sections.title: Formula SAE
paragraphs: Our main category, and the biggest one worldwide. It's fiercely contested across the Americas — Brazil, the United States — and in Europe too.
Formula SAE was born in 1981 at the University of Texas, led by professor Ron Matthews. The first edition had just 6 teams and 40 students.

journey.title: Before Formula, there is a journey.
journey.intro: UTN BA Motorsport is an integrated academy: every category adds complexity, responsibility and real experience. Nobody reaches the toughest project by accident.

items.title: First, learn by building.
items.text: New members design and build a kart. It is their first experience making technical decisions, manufacturing parts and understanding that every millimeter has a consequence.

items.title: Then, engineer under pressure.
items.text: In Baja SAE the challenge grows: a more complex vehicle, extreme conditions and a strict technical rulebook. Students train to interpret every requirement, document their decisions and pass inspections; they also work with safety components subject to FIA/SFI homologation whenever required by the rules.

items.title: Finally, build the car that represents us.
items.text: The electric Formula SAE car brings every lesson together. It is our most ambitious project: a single-seater designed, manufactured and assembled by students to compete in Brazil.

steps.title: We meet

design.title: Design
design.subtitle: CAD and engineering
design.body: Defines the geometry of the car. From the chassis to the suspension, every part is modelled in CAD before it exists: this is where the car takes shape and where everything that gets built later is prepared.

chemistry.title: Chemistry
chemistry.subtitle: Materials and compounds
chemistry.body: Handles materials: which compound goes into each part, how it behaves and how it is treated. This is the area that answers what the car is made of.

manufacturing.title: Manufacturing
manufacturing.subtitle: Build and assembly
manufacturing.body: Where the design becomes a car. Cutting, welding, machining and assembly: this is where every part is physically built and the car is put together.

cnc.title: CNC
cnc.subtitle: Precision machining
cnc.body: Makes the parts that leave no room for error. Uprights, hubs, bushings and suspension clamps come out of here: the components that hold the wheel and feed its loads into the chassis, machined under numerical control from the Design team's models. A tenth of a millimetre out of tolerance gets paid for on track.

industrial.title: Industrial
industrial.subtitle: Manufacturing and processes
industrial.body: Plans how everything gets done: schedules, processes, costs and suppliers. It is what keeps the project inside the calendar and the budget.

electronics.title: Electronics
electronics.subtitle: Hardware and firmware
electronics.body: Everything that carries current. Sensors, wiring, control and the firmware that runs them: in an electric car this is the nervous system of the project.

communication.title: Communications
communication.subtitle: Visual identity and social
communication.body: Tells the story of what the team does. Visual identity, social media, content and the relationship with sponsors: it is the face of the project.

teamPage.title: We are the first generation
teamPage.intro: Students at UTN Buenos Aires building, from scratch, the university's first electric Formula SAE car.
storyParagraphs: UTN BA Motorsport is a multidisciplinary team of students from Universidad Tecnológica Nacional, Facultad Regional Buenos Aires. Mechanical, electronic, electrical, industrial, systems and chemical engineering all work on the same project: a fully electric car to compete at Formula SAE Brazil 2027.

We are the first Formula SAE generation at UTN BA. That means we inherited neither a car nor a manual: we are writing both. Everything decided now is the starting point for the teams that come after us.
We believe the best way to learn engineering is by building it. Here what you study at university gets applied to a real part, with a real competition date and real consequences if it does not work.

carPage.intro: Designed, built and taken to the track by students at UTN Buenos Aires, to compete at Formula SAE Brazil 2027.
carPage.renderAlt: Render of the UTN BA Motorsport electric Formula SAE car
carPage.renderCaption: Working render of the car. The design is still evolving.
projectParagraphs: This is the team's first car, and it starts from zero: there is no previous season to copy a chassis from or reuse a battery pack. Every design decision is being made for the first time at UTN BA.
We chose electric from the start. It is the fastest growing category in Formula Student over the last decade, and the closest to the industry the people on this team will work in.
carPage.specsNote: The full spec sheet (mass, power, battery, suspension, tyres) is published as the design gets frozen. We don't put out numbers that can still change.
